extracted.intended_audience: empirical researchers/economists studying peer effects in education (readers of NBER-style empirical papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Specification, estimation, and reporting standards for regressions estimating peer effects on pupil reading scores (including WLS, clustering, IVs, controls, robustness checks, and reporting of tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sampling-probability weights (WLS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Weighted least squares regressions using students’ sampling probability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All regressions are weighted by the students’ sampling probability (WLS). Reporting indicates which columns use these weights. When correcting for sampling bias an explicit correction factor ((N-1)/(n-1)) is applied in some specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cluster standard errors at the school level
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard errors are robust to clustering at the school level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report standard errors in parentheses. Throughout tables the authors state that standard errors are clustered at the school level to account for within-school correlation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-level control variables to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Student level variables are student’s sex and age, parents’ origin, language spoken at home, index/number of books at home and number of persons living in household.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these individual covariates in baseline and augmented specifications to account for compositional differences across students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class-level control variables to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Class level variables are class size, class size squared, teacher’s sex, education, experience and experience squared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include class-level covariates (and squared terms where noted) to control for classroom environment and teacher characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: School-level control variables to include
rubrics_metrics.description: School level variables are community size, average daily instruction hours, shortage of staff, teaching material and buildings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These school characteristics are included to capture school environment differences that may confound peer effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include school peer variables
rubrics_metrics.description: School peer variables are school averages of index of number of books at home and parents’ origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controlling for school-level peer averages separates within-school/class peer composition effects from broader school peer patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use school fixed effects and class-level specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Run regressions at the class level or include school fixed effects. The fourth row refers to regressions of peer variables on class variables controlling for school fixed effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare specifications with and without school fixed effects; also estimate regressions aggregated to the class level as a robustness check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and treat tracked schools consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracked schools are those for which principals state that fourth-grade classes are formed on the basis of ability. Some specifications exclude tracked schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify tracked schools via principal responses and run robustness checks excluding them (since tracking can induce endogenous sorting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test independence of peer characteristics and class assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Pearson Chi² tests for independence of peer characteristic and class room assignment within each school using individual level data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also report p-values from Wald tests for joint significance of groups of variables (class, school, class+school). The first four rows in each panel report p-values of Wald tests, and the fifth row the Pearson Chi² p-value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report number of observations and weighting/estimation details
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of observations is reported (e.g., 4,577); regressions are weighted; standard errors clustered at school level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report sample size, weighting scheme, and standard-error treatment alongside coefficient estimates (standard errors shown in parentheses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative peer measures and robustness (parents’ education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peers’ index of parents’ highest education can be used as an alternative peer composition variable; compare results across different peer measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present alternative specifications (e.g., peers’ books vs peers’ parents’ education) and show how coefficients change to assess robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction specifications with individual family background
rubrics_metrics.description: Include interaction term of peers’ index and an individual-level dummy for >100 books at home; jointly include peer index and interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate how peer effects vary by individual family background by adding interaction terms and report joint inclusion results (columns labeled 'Peer' and 'Inter').

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental-variables strategy and instruments used
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual’s and peers’ index of number of books at home from the home questionnaire are instrumented by the individual’s and peers’ index of books at home from the student questionnaire and individual’s and peers’ index of parents’ highest educational level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume independent measurement errors (cov(u,u1)=0). Add a dummy for missing parental education to avoid sample-size loss. Report IV estimates and provide standard errors clustered at school level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction for sampling bias in IV specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The correction factor for sampling bias in some IV columns is (N-1)/(n-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply and report this correction when necessary; indicate which columns use the correction and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make assumptions about measurement error explicit and discuss bias directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement error is assumed classical so that measured variable = true + u, E(u)=0. The appendix derives plim expressions showing how measurement error and within-class sampling affect bias (attenuation and possible positive bias from omitted components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss special cases (no measurement error, whole-class sampled, only measurement error) and explain when attenuation or positive bias dominates. Use these analytical results to motivate robustness checks (e.g., IVs, sampling whole class where possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: If using IVs, require independent second measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments are based on an independent measurement of xics (cov(uics,u1ics)=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct z1 and z2 from independent questionnaires (student vs home) and show covariances; note the required independence for instrument validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report effect-size calculation transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect sizes: Column (3) is the square root of the covariance between the peer variables index of books at home taken from the student and the home questionnaire. Results in column (5) are calculated as (4)*(3)/(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the components used to compute standardized effect sizes (SD of test score, SD of peer variable, adjusted SD, peer effect estimate) and show the arithmetic used to derive the final effect size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report weighted means, standard deviations, and missing-data percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide weighted mean values (standard deviations in parentheses) for covariates and separate tables for percentage of missing values by variable and country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight means by sampling probability, show SDs, and list missingness rates to be transparent about data quality and potential biases from missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present regressions in a sequence of nested specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables present a sequence of specifications adding student-level, class-level, school-level, school peer variables, school fixed effects, and exclusion of tracked schools (columns (1)-(5) etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nested models to show how coefficient estimates change when additional controls or fixed effects are added; interpret stability across specifications as evidence of robustness.
